channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Science Over Stigma: Why Legislators Must Embrace Tobacco Harm Reduction
item.description: The text argues that growing evidence supports tobacco harm reduction products, especially e-cigarettes, as alternatives for adult smokers. It cites a Cochrane review of nine trials finding vaping more effective than traditional nicotine replacement therapies for quitting, with no serious harms identified in those trials. It also describes FDA authorization of reduced-risk marketing claims for ZYN nicotine pouches. The author contends that restrictive policies discourage cessation and fuel illicit markets, while cigarette smoking causes substantial mortality and economic costs. The text urges clinicians and policymakers to prioritize scientific evidence over stigma and prohibition, arguing that access to lower-risk nicotine products could improve public health. (Published on October 02, 2026byprotectingtaxpayers.org)

item.title: Illogical cancer plan will tax all nicotine products the same, while only labelling the carcinogen in your glass
item.description: The European Parliament’s public health committee approved a non-binding cancer policy report calling for higher, converging minimum taxes on all tobacco and nicotine products, while favouring labelling and awareness measures for alcohol and ultra-processed foods. Critics, including Czech MEP Tomáš Kubín, argue this approach ignores differing product risks, undermines harm reduction and conflicts with Parliament’s recent cardiovascular policy. They advocate evidence-based regulation, strict protections for minors and differentiated taxes encouraging healthier alternatives. Health economist Franco Sassi also calls for smarter food taxation to reduce cancer risks. The article urges Parliament to correct these perceived inconsistencies during the expected October–November plenary vote. (Published on October 02, 2026byparliamentnews.co.uk)

item.title: FDA’s common sense approach to tobacco regulation
item.description: The article portrays FDA tobacco director Bret Koplow as shifting regulation toward harm reduction after years of approval backlogs and limited support for cigarette alternatives. Speaking at a tobacco retailers’ conference, Koplow advocated cooperation with manufacturers and retailers to protect minors, accelerate authorization of scientifically supported lower-risk products for adults, and combat illicit e-cigarettes. His authorization of vaping and nicotine pouch products has drawn praise from industry and opposition from public health groups. Koplow emphasizes that no tobacco product is safe and quitting is healthiest, but completely switching from cigarettes to FDA-authorized, noncombustible alternatives can reduce exposure to toxic and cancer-causing chemicals. (Published on October 02, 2026bycspdailynews.com)

item.title: Smoking Is Bad for You. Nicotine Isn't—but Politicians Keep Trying To Ban It.
item.description: Easthampton became Massachusetts’ 25th municipality to adopt a lifetime nicotine-sales ban for younger generations, including noncombustible products. The author argues these policies conflate nicotine with smoking’s combustion-related harms and undermine harm reduction. Nicotine is addictive and carries cardiovascular and adolescent risks, but research suggests potential cognitive benefits, though therapeutic evidence remains preliminary. Comparing nicotine with caffeine and accepted nicotine-replacement therapies, the text criticizes restrictions on adult choice and the goal of eliminating nicotine use rather than smoking-related disease. It also warns that prohibition could encourage poorly studied, potentially stronger synthetic alternatives. The author advocates distinguishing nicotine from cigarettes and weighing its risks and benefits rather than treating it as inherently unacceptable. (Published on October 02, 2026byreason.com)

item.title: UK Vaping Duty Takes Effect
item.description: The UK’s Vaping Products Duty began October 1, charging £2.20 per 10ml of vaping liquid, including nicotine-free products. Duty stamps become mandatory for all products sold from April 1, 2027, after a grace period for existing stock. Non-compliance risks seizures, fines and criminal penalties. The government aims to discourage vaping among young people and nonsmokers, alongside higher tobacco duties. Industry representatives warn higher prices could drive consumers toward smoking or illicit products and increase retailers’ compliance burdens. The duty is projected to raise over £550 million annually by 2030–31, while £30 million annually through 2028–29 will support enforcement against illicit and underage tobacco and vape sales. (Published on October 02, 2026bytobaccoreporter.com)
